newsitem.title: FRANCE: French premier welcomes Papon war crimes trial.
newsitem.headline: French premier welcomes Papon war crimes trial.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe welcomed on Friday the Supreme Court's decision to send former cabinet minister Maurice Papon to trial on charges of crimes against humanity for deporting 1,560 Jews in 1942-44.
A lawyer representing the families of deportees said the trial would most likely begin in October or November and last three to four months.

Juppe, who is also mayor of Bordeaux, where Papon, 86, allegedly sent Jews on their way to Nazi death camps, urged his country to "face its past with lucidity" and called for light to be shed on who was responsible.
"I am simply pleased that justice is done," Juppe told reporters.
"The responsibilities must be established and all light must be shed on such a painful period of our history...I believe that France must face its past with lucidity," Juppe said.
Papon's trial, ordered by the Supreme Court on Thursday after a legal marathon of more than 15 years, will probably be France's last chance to put wartime Nazi collaboration in the dock.
Public prosecutors have built up a 50,000-page case against Papon, who was secretary-general of the Bordeaux prefect's office under the collaborationist Vichy government.
The Supreme Court ruled that Papon knew that deporting the Jews to the Drancy transit camp outside Paris would lead them inevitably to their deaths.

Lawyer Gerard Boulanger, who represents civil plaintiffs, said the exact date for a trial had not yet been set. "People are talking about October or November. We're going to fight for the trial to take place as soon as possible in the autumn.

"I think the trial will last between three and four months. For (Nazi officer Klaus) Barbie, it took two and a half months in Lyon in 1987. That case had many witnesses. I don't know how many witnesses there will be, but I do know that there are infinitely more written documents," Boulanger said.
